back: If sin y = x, then y = sin⁻¹x. The inverse function gives the angle whose trig ratio is known.
sin⁻¹x + cos⁻¹x = π/2 for x ∈ [−1,1]. This is the most useful property.
sin⁻¹(−x) = −sin⁻¹x (odd), cos⁻¹(−x) = π − cos⁻¹x (not simply even/odd), tan⁻¹(−x) = −tan⁻¹x (odd).
tan⁻¹x + tan⁻¹y = tan⁻¹((x+y)/(1−xy)) for xy < 1. If xy > 1, add or subtract π based on signs.
x ∈ [−1,1]. The sine function only outputs values in [−1,1], so the inverse accepts only these.
x ∈ ℝ. The tangent function outputs all real numbers, so the inverse accepts all reals.
sin(tan⁻¹x) = x/√(1+x²). Use right triangle: opposite=x, adjacent=1, hypotenuse=√(1+x²).
If θ ∈ [0,π], cos⁻¹(cos θ) = θ. Otherwise, find the reference angle in [0,π] with same cosine.
